/practice-areas.title: Choose a guide by the question you need answered
paragraphs: Start with the event if you are trying to identify who handled the report or what evidence may be available. A car crash, a fall at a store and an injury during a rideshare trip can leave very different records. Start with the injury if your concern is how to describe your treatment, work restrictions or the effect on daily tasks.

Write down one question before opening a guide. For example, “Who kept the camera recording?” leads to a narrower search than “How much is my case worth?” If you have a letter or a proposed release, keep its response date where you can see it as you read.

/practice-areas/personal-injury.title: The timeline when symptoms change over time
paragraphs: Start your chronology with the incident and add each medical visit, work change and new restriction by date. If you returned to work and later needed different duties, preserve both records. If a family member took over childcare or errands, record when it started and what they did. A timeline that includes improvements and setbacks lets a reviewer see what changed and which period needs better documentation.

For a general personal injury claim, keep four questions separate: what happened, who may be responsible, what the injury changed, and which insurance or other resources may apply. A photograph may help with the first question without answering the others. Label each item by the question it supports instead of sending an undated collection of files.

An insurance claim and a civil lawsuit are different steps. If you are trying to understand how to file a personal injury claim in California, the general guide below explains the distinction and how to organize a first submission. If the injury happened while working, identify that fact early so the workers’ compensation process and any separate claim can be considered on their own terms.

/practice-areas/car-accidents.title: What to save when the drivers disagree about a lane change
paragraphs: Keep any dashcam clip that shows the vehicles before impact. Record the road, direction of travel, lane markings and where the first contact occurred. Take wider vehicle photos that show where the damage sits relative to each door or wheel. If the insurer attributes the crash to one driver’s movement, ask which frames, statements or observed damage support that account.

A lane-change dispute can continue even after a carrier agrees to pay a repair bill. Keep the written fault explanation with the version of the report and images the adjuster actually received. If you send additional evidence, record when it was delivered and ask which disputed point remains unresolved. An offer, a payment and an explanation of responsibility are different records.

For an injury consultation, bring a short treatment timeline and any work restriction alongside the collision file. Include the decision you need help making now: an insurer’s request for records, a proposed release, or a bill due while the claim remains open. That makes the next discussion more focused than starting with an unsupported settlement estimate.
/practice-areas/car-accidents.linkLabel: Read how California handles shared fault

links.label: Making a claim when no police report is available
Organizing medical bills while the injury claim is pending

/practice-areas/truck-accidents.title: Identify the truck and the trailer separately
paragraphs: A tractor, trailer and cargo can be managed by different businesses. If you can safely record identifying details, keep the unit or plate numbers for both vehicles, along with any carrier name and the investigating agency’s report number. Write down where the contact occurred on the trailer or tractor. Those details can help determine whose records may show the vehicle’s route, inspection or dispatch instructions.

A company name painted on a trailer is a useful starting point, not a complete explanation of who controlled the driver or equipment. Preserve the name exactly as recorded and keep any identifiers from the collision paperwork. If an insurer or investigator later supplies another business name, retain that correspondence with its source and date.

Give the office the location and time of the crash and identify any inspection, towing or storage decision that is approaching. Company records and physical vehicle evidence may be held by different people. The first consultation can identify which missing information matters to the next decision and which records may require a preservation request.
/practice-areas/truck-accidents.linkLabel: See what records a truck crash can leave

links.label: Truck records, electronic logs and evidence preservation
Organizing your own collision and injury records

/practice-areas/motorcycle-accidents.title: Document the approach to the collision
paragraphs: When a driver says a rider appeared suddenly, the part that matters may be the few seconds before impact. Save an uninterrupted video if one exists. Record the direction of travel, any parked vehicles or obstructions and where each person was able to see cross traffic. Keep photos of the motorcycle and riding equipment before repairs or disposal. Different records answer questions about visibility, contact and injury.

Keep an inventory of the motorcycle, helmet, clothing and any accessories damaged in the collision. Record who currently holds each item and whether an inspection has been requested. A repair estimate can describe replacement costs without preserving the physical evidence, so ask about that distinction before equipment is discarded or work begins.

The motorcycle policy, another driver’s policy and the rider’s health coverage can answer different payment questions. Bring the declarations and correspondence that apply to the collision date, even if a carrier has not made a decision. Describe a coverage question separately from a disagreement about riding position, visibility or the other vehicle’s movement.

links.label: Matching a motorcycle loss to the coverage being reviewed
What to organize after a motorcycle accident

/practice-areas/pedestrian-accidents.title: Record where the crossing began and ended
paragraphs: Mark the curb you left and the place you were trying to reach. Note the direction of any turning driver and which signal you could see. A single picture of the impact area may omit the view from the corner, landscaping or parked vehicles. Wider scene photos and a clear map pin can help a reviewer understand what was visible before contact.

A witness who saw the impact may not have seen the signal change or the pedestrian begin crossing. Keep the witness’s own description with their contact details and note which part of the event they observed. A careful account preserves uncertainty instead of turning a brief observation into a complete reconstruction.

If the route included a bus stop, parking lot or driveway, draw those features on the same sketch. Keep the place where treatment began separate from the collision location. If walking or standing remains difficult, note the effect on commuting and work tasks with any supporting medical restrictions for the consultation.
/practice-areas/pedestrian-accidents.linkLabel: Read what can matter in a pedestrian claim

links.label: Organizing a pedestrian collision and injury record

/practice-areas/rideshare-accidents.title: Preserve the trip record if the ride ended early
paragraphs: Save the booking receipt even if the driver canceled or ended the ride after the crash. Keep messages about the pickup or drop-off location, plus the time the trip appeared to start or end in the app. If the passenger and the person who booked the trip differ, ask the account holder to keep the original record. Put the actual collision time in a separate entry.

An app receipt can identify a booked trip without showing every event during the collision. Preserve the original messages, the trip identifier and any notice that the ride was canceled or refunded. If your account no longer shows the trip, keep the support request and response rather than treating a missing screen as proof that no ride existed.

Separate correspondence from the platform, the driver’s insurer and your own carrier. Record which loss each person is reviewing and whether they requested a statement, medical record or inspection. Send the same date and trip identifiers with each relevant request so a coverage disagreement does not become a disagreement about which event is being discussed.
/practice-areas/rideshare-accidents.linkLabel: Read about rideshare coverage and trip status

links.label: Which trip records matter to Uber and Lyft coverage
Preparing questions after a rideshare collision

/practice-areas/slip-and-fall.title: Identify who controlled the exact spot
paragraphs: Write down whether you fell inside the store, on a shared walkway or in the parking lot. A store employee may have taken your report even when another business maintained that part of the property. Save a receipt or check-in record that helps establish the time, and take a wider photo showing the route. Ask for the report reference and record who responded.

If the condition was cleaned or repaired after the fall, keep the photograph or message that shows when that happened. Record who told you about earlier complaints or inspections and distinguish their statement from something you saw yourself. A change to the area does not, on its own, resolve what the property operator knew before the incident.

Bring the incident reference, location sketch, available photographs and treatment chronology to the consultation. If an insurer asks for a broad release or a recorded account, keep the request in its original form so the scope can be discussed. A consultation can begin even when the business has not provided its internal report.
/practice-areas/slip-and-fall.linkLabel: Read a court example about store inspections

links.label: Evidence and notice questions after a fall
Organizing an injury claim before submitting records

/practice-areas/wrongful-death.title: Organize practical records without sharing more than necessary
paragraphs: Families can start with a private list of who has each record. Note where to find the incident report, funeral invoices, employment or benefits paperwork, and any insurer correspondence. Keep a record of who has been asked to respond or sign. An initial message can describe the incident and what paperwork has arrived. A detailed family or medical record can stay private until the office explains what it needs and how to send it.

When more than one relative is helping, choose a way to avoid duplicate or conflicting requests. One person can maintain a list of documents received without assuming authority to sign a release for the family. Mark who supplied each record and whether it is a complete copy. Tell the office about any estate proceeding or lawyer already involved.

Financial support can include more than a pay statement. Preserve records showing recurring household payments and describe practical help the person provided, such as regular transportation or caregiving. Keep observed contributions separate from estimates about the future. Howard can review which relationships, losses and claim procedures need legal analysis before a demand or signature is considered.

links.label: Questions to prepare for a wrongful death consultation
Understanding the different records in a wrongful death claim

/practice-areas/serious-injuries.title: Record what support a discharge plan actually requires
paragraphs: Keep the discharge instructions with a short account of the help someone needed at home. Note transportation, appointments, equipment and any tasks the family had to take over. If the plan changes after a follow-up appointment, save the newer guidance and when it took effect. Separating a recommendation from what happened at home helps explain both the care plan and its day-to-day impact.

When relatives are coordinating care, keep a dated list of appointments, recommended equipment and changes to the home routine. Identify whether help was recommended by a professional, provided by a family member, or still being arranged. This gives a reviewer a clearer picture than a single total for all care-related spending.

For concentration, memory or fatigue concerns, record the task affected and when the change was observed. Keep those observations separate from a diagnosis or prediction about recovery. Bring the relevant evaluations and work restrictions so the discussion can identify what is documented and which medical or financial questions remain open.
/practice-areas/serious-injuries.linkLabel: Read more about long-term care records

links.label: Documenting the effects of a possible brain injury
How records support an injury claim valuation

/es/practice-areas.title: Elija la guía según lo que necesita averiguar
paragraphs: Si busca identificar quién hizo un informe o qué grabación puede existir, empiece por el tipo de accidente. Si su pregunta se refiere a las limitaciones en el trabajo o en casa, empiece por la lesión. Tenga a mano la carta del seguro y anote su fecha de respuesta antes de leer sobre ese trámite.
/es/practice-areas.linkLabel: Explore las guías por lesión (en inglés)

/ko/practice-areas.title: 확인하려는 내용에 맞는 안내 선택하기
paragraphs: 누가 보고서를 작성했는지, 영상 자료가 어디에 있을지 알고 싶다면 사고 유형부터 확인하세요. 직장이나 집에서 어떤 활동이 어려워졌는지가 궁금하다면 부상 유형 안내부터 살펴보세요. 보험사 서류가 있다면 관련 절차를 읽기 전에 회신 날짜를 먼저 적어 두세요.

/es/practice-areas/car-accidents.title: Qué conservar cuando se discute un cambio de carril
paragraphs: Guarde el video que muestre la aproximación de ambos vehículos antes del impacto. Anote el sentido, las marcas de los carriles y el primer punto de contacto. Tome fotografías amplias que ubiquen el daño respecto de una puerta o una rueda. Si el seguro atribuye el choque a una maniobra, pregunte qué registro respalda esa versión.
/es/practice-areas/car-accidents.linkLabel: Lea cómo se reparte la culpa

/ko/practice-areas/car-accidents.title: 차로 변경을 두고 진술이 엇갈릴 때
paragraphs: 충돌 전 두 차량이 접근하는 모습이 담긴 영상을 보관하세요. 진행 방향, 차선 표시, 처음 맞닿은 지점을 기록하세요. 파손 부위를 문이나 바퀴와 함께 찍어 위치가 드러나게 하세요. 특정 차량의 움직임이 원인이라는 답변을 받았다면 어떤 자료에 근거했는지 물어보세요.

/es/practice-areas/truck-accidents.title: Identifique el tractocamión y el remolque por separado
paragraphs: Conserve los números de unidad o placas de ambos, el nombre visible de la empresa y la referencia del informe. Anote en qué parte del vehículo ocurrió el primer contacto. Estos detalles ayudan a identificar quién podría tener los registros de la ruta, la inspección o el despacho.
/es/practice-areas/truck-accidents.linkLabel: Vea qué registros puede dejar un choque de camión

/ko/practice-areas/truck-accidents.title: 트랙터와 트레일러를 각각 확인하세요
paragraphs: 트랙터와 트레일러의 차량 번호나 등록번호, 확인한 운송사 이름, 사고 보고서 번호를 따로 적어 두세요. 어느 부분이 처음 맞닿았는지도 남기세요. 이 정보는 운행 기록이나 점검 자료, 배차 정보를 어느 회사가 갖고 있는지 알아보는 데 도움이 됩니다.
/ko/practice-areas/truck-accidents.linkLabel: 트럭 사고에서 확인할 수 있는 기록 보기

/es/practice-areas/motorcycle-accidents.title: Documente cómo se acercaron los vehículos
paragraphs: Cuando alguien dice que la moto apareció de repente, el video de los segundos previos puede aclarar la visibilidad. Anote el sentido de marcha y cualquier vehículo estacionado u obstáculo. Conserve fotografías de la moto y del equipo antes de reparar o desechar algo.
/es/practice-areas/motorcycle-accidents.linkLabel: Lea las preguntas sobre choques de motocicleta (en inglés)

/ko/practice-areas/motorcycle-accidents.title: 충돌 전 접근 경로를 기록하세요
paragraphs: 오토바이가 갑자기 나타났다는 진술이 있다면 충돌 전 몇 초를 보여 주는 영상이 시야를 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다. 주행 방향과 주차 차량, 시야를 가린 물체를 적어 두세요. 수리하거나 버리기 전에 오토바이와 장비 상태를 사진으로 남기세요.

/es/practice-areas/pedestrian-accidents.title: Marque dónde comenzó el cruce
paragraphs: Señale la acera desde la que salió, su destino y el sentido del auto que giraba. Anote qué señal podía ver. Una foto amplia tomada desde la esquina ayuda a ubicar vehículos estacionados, señales y otras obstrucciones antes del punto de impacto.
/es/practice-areas/pedestrian-accidents.linkLabel: Lea qué puede importar en un reclamo peatonal (en inglés)

/ko/practice-areas/pedestrian-accidents.title: 횡단을 시작한 위치부터 표시하세요
paragraphs: 출발한 연석, 향하던 곳, 회전 차량이 오던 방향을 표시하세요. 보였던 신호도 적어 두세요. 모퉁이에서 넓게 찍은 사진은 충돌 지점에 도달하기 전 주차 차량이나 표지판 때문에 시야가 어떻게 달랐는지 보여 줄 수 있습니다.
/ko/practice-areas/pedestrian-accidents.linkLabel: 보행자 사고 청구에서 중요한 내용 보기 (영어)

/es/practice-areas/rideshare-accidents.title: Guarde el registro si el viaje terminó antes de tiempo
paragraphs: Conserve el recibo y los mensajes sobre cambios en la recogida, aunque se haya cancelado el viaje después del choque. Guarde la hora que muestra la aplicación para cada cambio y anote la hora del choque por separado. Si otra persona pidió el viaje, pídale que conserve el original.
/es/practice-areas/rideshare-accidents.linkLabel: Lea sobre la cobertura según el estado del viaje

/ko/practice-areas/rideshare-accidents.title: 승차공유 운행이 일찍 끝나도 기록을 보관하세요
paragraphs: 사고 뒤 운행이 취소되었더라도 예약 영수증과 탑승 위치 변경 메시지를 보관하세요. 앱에 표시된 변경 시각과 실제 사고 시각을 따로 적어 주세요. 다른 사람이 차량을 호출했다면 그 사람에게 원본 기록을 보관해 달라고 하세요.
/ko/practice-areas/rideshare-accidents.linkLabel: 운행 상태와 승차공유 보험 안내 보기

/es/practice-areas/slip-and-fall.title: Identifique quién controlaba el punto de la caída
paragraphs: Anote si se cayó dentro de la tienda, en una zona común o en un estacionamiento. Guarde un recibo que ayude a establecer la hora y una fotografía amplia de su recorrido. Pregunte quién recibió el informe y cuál es su referencia.
/es/practice-areas/slip-and-fall.linkLabel: Lea un caso judicial sobre inspecciones de tiendas

/ko/practice-areas/slip-and-fall.title: 넘어진 장소를 누가 관리했는지 확인하세요
paragraphs: 매장 내부, 공용 통로, 주차장 중 어디에서 넘어졌는지 적어 두세요. 시간을 확인할 수 있는 영수증과 이동 경로가 담긴 넓은 사진을 보관하세요. 누가 사고를 접수했는지, 보고서 번호를 받을 수 있는지도 확인하세요.
/ko/practice-areas/slip-and-fall.linkLabel: 매장 점검에 관한 캘리포니아 판례 보기

/es/practice-areas/wrongful-death.title: Organice los documentos de la familia en privado
paragraphs: Hagan una lista de quién tiene el informe, las facturas funerarias y la correspondencia del seguro o del empleador. Anoten a quién se le pidió firmar o responder y en qué fecha. En el primer contacto, pueden mencionar qué papeles recibieron y preguntar cómo enviar lo que se necesite.

/ko/practice-areas/wrongful-death.title: 유가족이 가진 자료를 비공개로 정리하세요
paragraphs: 어떤 가족이 사고 보고서, 장례 비용 내역, 보험사나 고용주 서류를 가지고 있는지 목록을 만드세요. 누가 서명이나 회신을 요청받았고 그 날짜는 언제인지 적으세요. 첫 문의에서는 받은 서류와 급한 문제를 설명하고 안전한 자료 전달 방법을 확인하면 됩니다.

/es/practice-areas/serious-injuries.title: Anote la ayuda que exige el plan de alta
paragraphs: Guarde las instrucciones de alta y anote qué ayuda fue necesaria en casa, incluidos traslados, citas y equipo. Si cambian las recomendaciones, guarde la versión más reciente con la fecha en que empezó a aplicarse. Así puede explicar tanto el plan como lo que ocurrió en la práctica.
/es/practice-areas/serious-injuries.linkLabel: Lea sobre los registros de cuidado a largo plazo (en inglés)

/ko/practice-areas/serious-injuries.title: 퇴원 뒤 실제로 필요했던 도움을 기록하세요
paragraphs: 퇴원 안내문을 보관하고 통원, 장비 사용, 일상생활에서 어떤 도움을 받았는지 적으세요. 추후 진료에서 안내가 바뀌면 새 문서와 적용 시작 날짜를 남겨 두세요. 진료 계획과 집에서 실제로 받은 도움을 각각 설명할 수 있습니다.
/ko/practice-areas/serious-injuries.linkLabel: 장기 돌봄 기록에 관한 질문 보기 (영어)
